messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The dataset with the highest value for the hyperparameter λa is NYT Sports, with a value of 0.9." -- cites: E1 (Section Table 3): quote "NYT Sports (20, 15, 15) (0.9, 0.5, 0.7)"
2. "The Shootings dataset has a hyperparameter λa value of 0.3." -- cites: E1 (Section Table 3): quote "Shootings (10, 20,15) (0.3, 0.1, 0.7)"
3. "The MUC dataset has a hyperparameter λa value of 0.7." -- cites: E1 (Section Table 3): quote "MUC (15, 12, 12) (0.7, 0.7, 0.4)"

Cited evidence:
[E1] (text, Section Table 3, page 7): Table 3: Details of hyper-parameters set for dif- ferent datasets. Dataset (r1, r2, r3) (λa, λb, λc) Shootings (10, 20,15) (0.3, 0.1, 0.7) NYT Sports (20, 15, 15) (0.9, 0.5, 0.7) MUC (15, 12, 12) (0.7, 0.7, 0.4)

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E1 (Section Table 3) shows that the dataset NYT Sports has a hyperparameter λa value of 0.9.
The evidence in E1 (Section Table 3) shows that the dataset Shootings has a hyperparameter λa value of 0.3.
The evidence in E1 (Section Table 3) shows that the dataset MUC has a hyperparameter λa value of 0.7.
